direction: engine vocabulary → what World Forge can author
proofPack: @ai-rpg-engine/starter-merchant (Salt Road Ledger) — the economy starter, chosen because it exercises the living-economy surface the 2.5D charter calls the moat
headline: A pack is a FUNCTION, not a document. `PackEntry.createGame(seed?) => Engine` has no content field, so the ceiling on any JSON content contract is set by how much of a pack is code: module selection, module config, rulesets, hazard closures, event subscriptions, presentation rules and AI intent profiles are all unauthorable by construction, not by omission.

rows.subject: quests
rows.note: The engine validates quests as a first-class pack key and ships a quest module; World Forge has NO quest domain at all — not a schema type, not an editor surface, not a converter. The single largest authoring hole.

rows.subject: abilities
rows.note: AbilityDefinition drives the verb/status web validateGameContent builds. No forge equivalent.

rows.subject: statuses
rows.note: StatusDefinition (stacking, duration, modifiers, triggers, removal). No forge equivalent — the schema has no status vocabulary whatsoever.

rows.subject: verbs
rows.note: The forge CAN name verbs — item.grantedVerbs, archetype.grantedVerbs, discipline.grantedVerb — but cannot DEFINE one. It emits dangling references into a slot it never fills.

rows.subject: archetypes
rows.note: The one bright spot: buildCatalog.archetypes IS authored and IS exported. It lands under `buildCatalog`, a key the engine ContentPack does not declare, so the intake still cannot see it — an authoring win cancelled by a wire gap.

rows.subject: backgrounds
rows.note: Same shape as archetypes: authored, exported, and delivered to a key the engine type does not declare.

rows.subject: itemUseEffects
rows.note: Bespoke item-use effects. The forge authors item STATS but no use effects; merchant authors one as a JS object with a `use` function (content.ts:144) — see the pack-code rows.

rows.subject: ZoneState.roomId
rows.note: REQUIRED by ZoneState, absent from ZoneDefinition. Any future converter must invent a value, which is exactly why no converter exists yet. Measured inert in all twelve worlds — a required field nothing reads.

rows.subject: ZoneState.stability
rows.note: ALIVE and unauthorable. district-core.ts:348 aggregates zone stability into district stability; rumor-propagation.ts:226 gates rumour spread on it; cognition-core.ts:1173 and observer-presentation.ts:395 read it. Measured moving four of twelve worlds. No pack file can set it.

rows.subject: ZoneState.authority
rows.note: Zero readers repo-wide AND absent from ZoneDefinition. Unauthorable and unread — the only field in this table that is dead on both sides.

rows.subject: createGame(seed)
rows.note: THE STRUCTURAL FINDING. A pack IS a function that builds an Engine — chooses modules, wires config, adds zones and entities, subscribes to events. `PackEntry` has no content field. No amount of JSON can express a pack, because a pack is not data.

rows.subject: hazard closures
rows.note: environment-core calls `hazard.condition(zone, entity, world)` and `hazard.effect(...)`. Both are JS functions the pack supplies (starter-merchant/src/setup.ts:176-196 authors two). A hazard STRING in a zone means whatever a closure says it means, and nothing otherwise — proven by the hazard pair in P2.

rows.subject: module selection + config
rows.note: Which of the engine's modules run, and how each is configured, is a code decision: buildCombatStack statMapping, buildWorldStack factions/cohesion, createPerceptionFilter perceptionStat, createAbilityCore statMapping, createContractCore catalog + status injectors. The forge has no vocabulary for any of it.

rows.subject: rulesets
rows.note: RulesetDefinition is a PackEntry field with no forge counterpart. The export lane hard-codes `ruleset: 'standard-v1'` in the manifest (convert-pack.ts:82) regardless of what the pack would need.

rows.subject: event subscriptions
rows.note: Packs subscribe to the live event bus in createGame — merchant grants the guild seal on `dialogue.ended`. Content-as-data has no way to say "when X happens, do Y" outside the narrow ConditionSpec/EffectDefinition vocabulary.

rows.subject: presentation rules
rows.note: A presentation rule carries `condition` and `transform` closures over the event stream. Pure code.

rows.subject: intent profiles
rows.note: Per-NPC AI intent profiles with `evaluate` functions. The forge authors `ai.profileId` as a bare string; the behaviour behind the string is code.

rows.subject: QuestDefinition (3 quests, staged)
rows.note: open-the-books / the-late-caravan / the-standing-account, each with stages, objectives, rewards and gating. WorldProject has no quest type at all.

rows.subject: AbilityDefinition (3 abilities)
rows.note: read-the-room / call-the-debt / cut-losses, with costs, targets and effects.

rows.subject: StatusDefinition set
rows.note: The pack's statuses, including `encumbered`, which contract-core applies via injected apply/remove.

rows.subject: EncounterDefinition + spawn tables
rows.note: The forge authors `encounterAnchors` — a raw pass-through key with ZERO engine hits. The engine's real encounter vocabulary (compositions, participants, validZoneTags, per-zone tables) is entirely unauthorable.

rows.subject: BossDefinition + phase listener
rows.note: Boss phases. The forge can tag an entity `boss`; it cannot say what a boss DOES.

rows.subject: District.baseMetrics.commerce as economy driver
rows.note: AUTHORABLE AND CARRIED — one of the few live economy levers the lane transports. Merchant's own comment records that leaving it at the default 50 made `recovery` opportunities unfireable catalog-wide.

rows.subject: economyGenre / tradeGenre / craftingGenre
rows.note: Three separate genre keys selecting supply tables, buyable stock and recipes. The forge has ONE free-text `genre` that maps only to packMeta.genres.

rows.subject: faction cohesion + membership
rows.note: buildWorldStack takes factions as {factionId, entityIds, cohesion}. The forge authors FactionPresence (districtIds, influence, alertLevel, patrolRoutes) — a raw pass-through with zero engine hits, and a different vocabulary entirely. The two systems do not share a single field name.

rows.subject: safeZoneTags / biasTags combat config
rows.note: Which zone tags mean "safe" is per-pack config. The forge authors tags but cannot say what any of them MEAN — which is why P2 measured tags live in only 8 of 12 worlds.

rows.subject: CurrencyReward / xpAwards
rows.note: Progression rewards with recipient predicates (functions).

rows.subject: ItemCatalog + transferGuard
rows.note: The forge authors item placements that become ItemDefinitions, but the catalog wiring and the consignment transfer guard (a closure) are code.

rows.subject: item chronicle recognition
rows.note: createItemChronicleCore takes an `evaluate` closure deciding when an instrument earns a name.

rows.subject: contract-core obligation clock
rows.note: A whole pack-local MODULE — five commerce verbs and an obligation clock. Packs can ship engine modules of their own; the forge cannot express a module.
